title: The view from the proving grounds for next-generation nuclear reactors, Atomic City, Idaho
description: A new generation of small nuclear reactors is poised to come online in the next few years. Public opinion remains split.

title: Fighting loneliness by filling empty chairs
description: When it comes to loneliness, sometimes the best medicine is just having someone to talk to. A global movement is bringing strangers together with a simple message: pull up a chair. Tina Kraus reports.

title: Extreme Heat Comes for the Red Chile Capital of Pakistan
description: The traditional ways of cultivating the peppers may not survive the challenges of climate change and soaring costs, so Pakistani farmers are trying to adapt.

title: Malaysia Was Confident in Its Social Media Ban, but Kids Are Still on TikTok
description: Officials told platforms to verify children’s ages using government-issued documents, like identity cards. But the companies have balked, apparently over privacy concerns.

title: He Transformed His Spanish Hometown. Did He Also Spoil It?
description: Francisco de la Torre, the mayor of Málaga, is credited with turning the once drab port into a culture and tech hub. Critics say he’s also destroyed the city’s soul.

title: How Spain’s migration surge tested E.U. border policy
description: An unprecedented surge of migrants into Spanish territory of Ceuta in North Africa marked the first  reignited the European Union’s debate over immigration.

title: Trump names Will Scharf as White House counsel ahead of midterms
description: Trump has named White House Staff Secretary Will Scharf as White House counsel, starting from September 1.

title: Yankees still waiting for Jazz Chisholm Jr. to ‘get dialed in’ as slump continues
description: The Yankees keep waiting for Jazz Chisholm Jr. to take off.

title: Victor Eklund putting in the work with battle Islanders roster spot ahead of him
description: The Islanders don’t want to rush their prospects, and as underwhelming as this offseason was, they will head into training camp about a month from now with a depth chart Victor Eklund will need to earn his way up.

title: Inside the new rise of trading cards
description: Interest in trading cards jumped during the pandemic, with folks digging through boxes in closets and garages to keep themselves busy. The industry is now worth an estimated $50 billion, but questions are rising about whether some of the more popular aspects of trading and collecting are actually gambling. Jarred Hill reports.
